newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to float five firms on bourse in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland to float five firms on bourse in 1997.

text.p: At least five companies should be privatised through flotation on the Warsaw bourse next year, deputy treasury minister in charge of privatisation, Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Thursday.
"We think of about five, maybe six public offerings next year," Kaczmarek told Reuters in an interview.

He said that the plan envisaged public offerings of Polar white goods maker, KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper concern, Swiecie paper maker, Impexmetal SA non-ferrous metals trader and Hutmen, a non-ferrous metals maker.

"These are not the only proposals as we also consider a public offering of Orbis (travel agency and hotels chain) next year and perhaps a capital increase in the Domy Towarowe Centrum (department store chain)," he said.

Kaczmarek, who had served as privatisation minister since 1993 in three leftist coalition cabinets, assumed his post on Tuesday in the newly created powerful treasury ministry, which encompassed his old portfolio.
